page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server designed for compute-heavy and graphics-intensive workloads. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, delivering 20 physical cores with 20 vCPUs under a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing 12.8 GB of memory per core. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, offering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, meaning storage must be attached externally.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance across both CPU and memory subsystems. The AMD EPYC 9575F processor achieves top-tier status in single-core stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, alongside strong multi-core performance in PassMark and Geekbench multi-core suites. Memory bandwidth is also highly competitive, placing in the top 25% for both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached read/write operations. In LLM inference tests, the server demonstrates top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds for small 135M models, and strong text generation speeds for medium 7B models, though prompt processing for 7B models falls into the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high resource density by combining a high-capacity 256 GB memory array with dual enterprise-grade L40S GPUs, making it a viable alternative to larger, more expensive multi-GPU nodes. However, a key tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, which requires users to factor in network-attached storage performance. This server is highly suited for workloads such as machine learning inference, data science, image processing, and high-throughput database operations.
